name: LanceDB
tagline: A database for vector, full-text, and hybrid retrieval with Rust, Python, TypeScript, and Java interfaces.
hook: A cross-language guide tracing table methods through native and remote code, bindings, Python APIs, generated code, and docs.
summary: LanceDB follows one table method from the Rust core through remote implementations and language bindings. The guide also warns about stale native extensions, hand-maintained API references, and documentation checks missing from pull-request CI.

techniques.title: Trace a feature across implementation boundaries
techniques.body: The new-method plan walks through the Table trait, native and remote implementations, Python binding layers, and TypeScript wrappers. It names tests and generated definitions at the steps where they become necessary.
techniques.quote:
Adding a new method involves first adding it to the Rust core, then exposing it
in the Python and TypeScript bindings. There are both local and remote tables.
Remote tables are implemented via a HTTP API and require the `remote` cargo
feature flag to be enabled. Python has both sync and async methods.

techniques.title: Rebuild a stale extension before declaring the environment blocked
techniques.body: Python validation uses the locked uv environment. Missing or stale Rust/PyO3 bindings have a prescribed rebuild path instead of being treated as final evidence that tests cannot run.
techniques.quote:
If `lancedb._lancedb`
is missing or stale, or if Rust/PyO3 binding code changed, rebuild the Python
extension with the bootstrap command above before running tests.

techniques.title: Expose what the documentation build does not discover
techniques.body: The Python API reference is hand-maintained. Some modules derive symbols from __all__, while others need individual directives, so a new public API can be silently absent from the rendered reference.
techniques.quote:
`docs/src/python/python.md` is the entire Python API reference. It is maintained by
hand, and anything not listed there is not rendered at all, so new public classes and
module-level functions have to be added explicitly.

techniques.title: Name the documentation check missing from PR CI
techniques.body: The guide supplies a local MkDocs build command after explaining reference-link syntax. It explicitly says the docs site only builds on main, preventing a green PR from being read as evidence that documentation renders.
techniques.quote: The docs site only builds on pushes to `main`, so this is not covered by PR CI.

steal: Show a representative feature crossing every public binding layer.
Give stale generated extensions a recovery procedure.
Explain which documentation symbols require manual registration.
State the verification gaps in a successful PR check run.
outline: Example plan: adding a new method on Table
